The AI Swarm broadcasts one AI-agent task to many servers at once. Each selected server gets its own independent agent run over its SSH session, and the per-server answers are combined into a single comparison table — one row per server — in a shared conversation.

Open it with KTPH003Tools KTPH011 AI Swarm...KTPH004 or KTPH005KTPH000KTPH006+KTPH007KTPH001KTPH008+KTPH009KTPH002KTPH010 (Cmd on macOS). The swarm opens as a regular tab, so terminals stay usable while a swarm runs.
The tab is split into three areas:
Animated orb per agent above the conversation — live state overview
One row per server with status badge, elapsed time, token count, and an expandable live transcript
The shared chat: your prompt, per-run progress, and the combined answer

The composer at the bottom (KTPH000Ask all selected servers…KTPH001) is a clearly framed, three-line input. KTPH002SendKTPH003 starts a run on every selected target; follow-up prompts continue the same conversation.

KTPH000Select servers…KTPH001 opens a picker over your saved connections. The target summary next to it shows how many servers are selected, how many already have an open terminal (KTPH002Open: nKTPH003), and how many will run without one (KTPH004Without terminal: nKTPH005).

Servers KTPH000without an open terminal are fully supportedKTPH001: the swarm opens a background SSH session for them on demand — no terminal tab is opened or required. This needs the master-password vault to be unlocked (the stored credentials are used), and the server key is accepted on first contact, the same trust model the terminal uses for new connections. KTPH002Connect missing (n)KTPH003 remains available as an explicit opt-in if you KTPH004wantKTPH005 terminals opened instead. KTPH006Include local shellKTPH007 adds your local machine to the swarm (local shells always need their open tab and are excluded from headless runs).
One orb per agent, colored and animated by state:
blue, pulsing with an orbiting dot
Agent is working; elapsed time ticks
An approval dialog is waiting for you
Paused via the run controls; the timer stops
blue with an amber ping ring
Running far longer than its peers (see below)
The run errored; details are in the agent row

KTPH001Adaptive slow detectionKTPH002 — an agent is flagged KTPH003unusually longKTPH004 when its elapsed time exceeds KTPH000; until at least two agents have finished, a fixed 180 s threshold applies. Paused and waiting agents are never flagged, and paused time is subtracted from the elapsed time, so the comparison stays fair.
f: max(60 s, 2 × median of the finished agents)

segments.t: While a run is active, KTPH000clicking an orbKTPH001 scrolls to and highlights that agent's row in the Agents list; hovering shows the server name and elapsed time. Legend chips below the orbs summarize the counts (running, waiting, paused, done, failed). After the run, the strip freezes at the final state.
The strip scales from a single server to large fleets — orbs shrink and pack into rows as the agent count grows:

Each server has a row in the KTPH000AgentsKTPH001 list showing its status badge, elapsed time, and token count. KTPH002Left-click a rowKTPH003 to expand it inline and watch the agent's live transcript (commands, output, and progress) while it runs — no extra window needed. Very long transcripts are trimmed from the front so the latest output is always visible.

KTPH000Right-click a rowKTPH001 for per-agent control: KTPH002PauseKTPH003, KTPH004ResumeKTPH005, KTPH006RestartKTPH007, and KTPH008StopKTPH009 apply to that agent only. Restarting one agent does not disturb the others; its answer is replaced in the combined result.

The toolbar offers the same four controls for the KTPH000whole swarmKTPH001: KTPH002PauseKTPH003, KTPH004ResumeKTPH005, KTPH006RestartKTPH007, and KTPH008StopKTPH009. Pausing is cooperative — each agent pauses at its next safe checkpoint (the badge shows KTPH010Pausing…KTPH011 until it takes effect), and elapsed timers stop while paused.
The KTPH000Read-onlyKTPH001 checkbox keeps every agent restricted to non-mutating commands. With read-only off, the KTPH002ApprovalKTPH003 policy decides how system-changing commands are confirmed:
The first agent that needs a change raises one dialog; KTPH000Approve on allKTPH001 covers every server in the run
Each server's changes are approved individually
The approval dialog also offers KTPH000Cancel swarmKTPH001 to stop the whole run.

When all agents finish, the swarm combines the per-server answers into one Markdown comparison table with exactly one row per server. The last column is always titled KTPH001"Fehler"KTPH002 and lists deviations, missing data, and errors (or KTPH000 when there is nothing to report), regardless of the response language.

Table cells are often too small for full command output — KTPH000click any table rowKTPH001 to open it in a separate KTPH002Row detailsKTPH003 window with a readable layout, KTPH004A− / A+KTPH005 font-size buttons, and a copy-to-clipboard button.

The conversation header has a KTPH000CopyKTPH001 button (whole conversation to the clipboard) and an KTPH002ExportKTPH003 menu with KTPH004Plain textKTPH005, KTPH006MarkdownKTPH007, and KTPH008PDFKTPH009. KTPH010SaveKTPH011 stores the conversation as a named swarm chat; saved swarm chats appear in a dedicated KTPH012Swarm ChatsKTPH013 section of the KTPH014AI ManagerKTPH015 and can be reopened later.

KTPH000Run script…KTPH001 executes a Snippet Manager script on KTPH002all swarm targets in parallel — without any AI involvementKTPH003. The dialog offers a searchable script picker (by name, category, language, or ID), a parameter field (one parameter per line), and a live summary; the KTPH004RunKTPH005 button is the single confirmation.

The script is transferred Base64-encoded (no quoting or special-character issues) and decoded on the server, with parameters passed as KTPH000, KTPH001, …. Progress appears in the same agent rows — expand a row to watch the live output — and the result is a per-server table with exit code and output. Non-POSIX shells (e.g. Windows targets) are skipped with a KTPH002Skipped: shell is not POSIXKTPH003 note while the rest of the swarm proceeds; unreachable servers are reported as KTPH004Not connectedKTPH005. KTPH006StopKTPH007 cancels a running script run.

The KTPH000WorkflowKTPH001 button turns the current swarm task into a single reusable multi-server script via the KTPH002Generate multi-server workflowKTPH003 dialog: choose the script language, the host-list source (selected connections, manual list, or external host file/inventory), and multi-server hardening options (parallel fan-out, per-host timeout, retry with backoff, aggregated end-of-run report, jump host, sudo/become, dry-run, and more).
KTPH000Syntax highlightingKTPH001 — the generated script is shown in a full editor with highlighting for the selected language.

KTPH000Visible progressKTPH001 — a working animation with a live elapsed counter (KTPH002Generating… 0:42KTPH003) while the AI works, and the total duration (KTPH004Done — took 1:37KTPH005) when it finishes.
KTPH000Additional instructionsKTPH001 — a three-line field for extra guidance the AI must follow, with a KTPH002HistoryKTPH003 menu of your last 10 distinct entries.
KTPH000Save to SnippetsKTPH001 — saves the script to the Snippet Manager with a fitting, pre-filled script name and the correct file extension.

KTPH001Hardening optionsKTPH002 — the same per-script KTPH003Hardening optionsKTPH004 as the single-host workflow generator (strict mode, error traps, idempotency, dry-run, KTPH000, and more) are applied to the generated script automatically with their all-on defaults; this dialog shows no panel for them. They are separate from the multi-server options above.

KTPH004Input hardeningKTPH005 — a collapsible KTPH006Input hardeningKTPH007 panel asks the AI to build an input-validation guard block into the generated script (parameter allowlists and length limits, file format checks, an adjustable KTPH000 limit, security warnings in the script's log, and a KTPH001 / KTPH002 override). The size check uses metadata before file content is read, and KTPH003 means unlimited. Strictly opt-in — the master check box starts unticked.
The AI Swarm tab itself shows a colored status dot, so you can watch progress from any other tab:
An agent is KTPH000waiting for your inputKTPH001
Run finished — stays until the next run starts

Swarm runs can execute unattended as KTPH000JobSchedulerKTPH001 jobs using the KTPH002AI SwarmKTPH003 action type. The KTPH004Schedule…KTPH005 button in the swarm toolbar is the fastest path: it opens the JobScheduler with a new job pre-filled from the current tab — the selected servers, the current prompt, the AI profile, and the read-only setting. The job is created disabled so you can review the schedule before enabling it.
Scheduled swarm jobs run completely headless over background SSH sessions — no terminal tabs are opened. Swarm-specific job fields:
The AI profile used for all agents in the run
The task broadcast to every target server
Approve system-changing commands without a dialog (unattended runs have nobody to ask)
How many servers run concurrently (1–16, default 4)
Restrict all agents to non-mutating commands (default: on)

Results land in KTPH000two placesKTPH001: the job KTPH002journalKTPH003 records the outcome per run, and the full conversation — including the combined comparison table — is stored as a KTPH004saved swarm chatKTPH005, so you can open it later from the AI Manager's KTPH006Swarm ChatsKTPH007 section and click through the result table like an interactive run. The scheduler's master-password and host-key gates apply as for other job types.
Recommended workflow: tune interactively, then schedule

Prompt quality decides result quality. Run the swarm interactively first, refine the prompt until the comparison table looks right, then click KTPH000Schedule…KTPH001 — the tuned prompt and target list carry over into the job.

KTPH000Nightly fleet health reportKTPH001 — a read-only prompt like KTPH002"Report disk usage, failed systemd units, and pending security updates"KTPH003 across all production servers every night; review the combined table each morning from the AI Manager.
KTPH000Configuration drift detectionKTPH001 — ask for the effective settings of a service on every host; deviations stand out in the per-server rows and the KTPH002FehlerKTPH003 column.
KTPH000Patch-level inventoryKTPH001 — collect kernel and package versions across the fleet on a weekly schedule and export the resulting table.

A scheduled swarm with KTPH000read-only offKTPH001 and KTPH002auto-approve onKTPH003 changes systems without anyone watching. Keep scheduled swarms read-only unless the prompt is deliberately designed (and tested interactively) to make changes.
